text: My idea was to attract the chivalry and nobility, and make them useful and keep them out of mischief. The plan worked very well, the competition for the places was hot. The conductor of the 4.33 express was a duke; there wasn't a passenger conductor on the line below the degree of earl. They were good men, every one, but they had two defects which I couldn't cure, and so had to wink at: they wouldn't lay aside their armor, and they would “knock down” fare --I mean rob the company. There was hardly a knight in all the land who wasn't in some useful employment.

provenance.work: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur's Court
provenance.author: Mark Twain
